# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about how to convey this manual to Blind, but I can only gesture to Deaf (who can see but not hear/touch). Blind can only feel the bomb, not see gestures or hear speech. So I cannot communicate directly with Blind at all.

The only path is: Mute → gestures → Deaf → speaks → Blind.

So I need to get this table to Deaf using gestures, and Deaf will need to figure out which light is currently lit (since Deaf can see the bomb), then relay to Blind which wire to cut, or relay the whole mapping so Deaf can combine it with what they see.

Since gestures carry no text/letters, I need to encode colors using a fixed symbol convention. Let me establish a mapping using gesture symbols to represent colors, in a consistent order matching the table rows so Deaf can parse it.

I'll wait this turn since I'm first to gesture but Deaf hasn't spoken yet and I have no context of what Deaf sees. Actually turn order is Blind, Mute, Deaf - so I go before Deaf. I should send the manual now via gestures, establishing a color code, since Deaf will read it right after me this round.

Let me define: 👍=blue, 👎=green, ☝=red, ✌=white, 🤟=yellow. Then send pairs (light, cut-color) in order.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎","🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟","☝"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 🖐]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 👍 👎 ✋ 🤟]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👌]

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👎","☝","✌","🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])

```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Display shows 0. Light is green. Wires in order 1 to 5 are: red, yellow, green, white, blue.
Blind says to Mute: I am ready. I can feel 5 wires but no colors or markings. Please tell me what the manual says to do, and relay anything Deaf has gestured about the display or light.

I now know: light is green → cut wire color yellow (per manual). Deaf reported wire order 1-5: red, yellow, green, white, blue. So the yellow wire is position 2.

I need to relay this to Blind, but I cannot speak to Blind at all - Blind cannot see my gestures, and I cannot speak. Blind can only be reached by touch (which I can't do) or hear speech from Deaf/others. Wait, actually let me recheck: Blind "cannot see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed" - but can Blind hear? The rules don't say Blind is deaf. Blind's restrictions are: cannot see. So Blind CAN hear speech. But I (Mute) cannot speak.

So I must relay through Deaf: I gesture to Deaf, Deaf speaks to Blind. Deaf already knows the wire order and light color themselves, and now needs to know the manual rule to compute which wire to cut, then tell Blind.

I already sent the full manual to Deaf via gestures last turn (color code: 👍=blue,👎=green,☝=red,✌=white,🤟=yellow; pairs blue→green, green→yellow, red→white, white→blue, yellow→red). Deaf should now be able to compute: light=green → cut yellow → wire position 2.

I'll wait, since Deaf should now compute and instruct Blind directly.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Still waiting to hear from you. What does the manual say? Any word from Deaf about the bomb's markings?

Deaf should have received my full color-coded manual by now (sent in turn 2, arriving turn 3) plus the light/wire info they reported. Deaf needs to combine: light=green → cut yellow → yellow is wire position 2, and tell Blind directly ("cut wire 2"). I cannot speak to Blind myself, so I can't answer Blind's question directly - only Deaf can, since Deaf is the one who can speak to Blind.

Let me gesture to Deaf again, confirming the answer plainly in case my earlier code wasn't parsed, to push them to act: I'll re-send the specific pair for green→yellow to make sure Deaf can finish the computation and speak to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎","🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","🤟"])
wait()
```

TURN 5

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |

| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I see wires two and five, then four and five. Do you mean cut two and five, or is five a fallback for both?

Deaf misread my gestures as instructions about which wires to cut, not as color-code definitions. I need to clarify. My gesture symbols were meant as a code: 👍=blue, 👎=green, ☝=red, ✌=white, 🤟=yellow. The pair (👎,🤟) meant "green→yellow" (light green means cut yellow wire), and (✌,🤟) meant "white→yellow" - wait that's wrong, let me recheck my own manual encoding.

Actually the manual says: white→blue, not white→yellow. I made an error in turn 4 - I sent ✌(white),🤟(yellow) which doesn't match any manual row correctly since white should map to blue (👍). Let me fix this now and resend clearly, one pair at a time, confirming receipt style.

Given the confusion, better approach: just tell Deaf directly and simply which wire to cut, since Deaf already told me the wire order and light color in turn 3. I compute it myself: light=green → cut yellow (from manual) → wire order was red,yellow,green,white,blue → yellow is position 2. I need Deaf to cut... no, Deaf can't touch. Deaf needs to relay "cut wire 2" to Blind via speech.

I'll send a very explicit single gesture sequence representing just the number 2, using a clear numeral-gesture convention, plus my color key resend to fix the earlier error.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I don't understand three three then stop. Please gesture wire numbers one at a time, slowly, using the code: thumbs up for one, thumbs down for two, index finger for three, peace sign for four, love sign for five.
Blind says to Mute: No response received yet on my end. If you can hear this, please share the manual's instructions - specifically what determines a safe wire to cut. I have 5 wires I can feel but no distinguishing marks reach me by touch.

Deaf has proposed a clear numeral code: 👍=1, 👎=2, ☝=3, ✌=4, 🤟=5. This is exactly what I need - I want to say "cut wire 2" (since yellow is position 2 in the order red,yellow,green,white,blue, and light=green requires cutting yellow).

Let me use Deaf's own code to send the single number 2, unambiguously, one gesture only.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | white |

| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Understood, wire two, yellow. Is that the wire to cut? Should Blind cut only wire two, or are there more steps like checking light or display first?

Deaf now correctly understands: wire two (yellow) is the one to cut. This matches my calculation (light=green → manual says cut yellow → yellow is wire position 2). This is the only step needed based on the manual - no other conditions. I should confirm clearly.

Since I can't speak to Blind directly, I need Deaf to relay "cut wire 2" to Blind. I'll confirm to Deaf with a clear affirmative gesture and the number again to be safe, so Deaf proceeds to tell Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

|---|---|

| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Understood: yes cut wire two, no other steps needed. I will stay ready in case something changes after the cut.

Good, Deaf now has the correct instruction and should relay "cut wire 2" to Blind. My job here is done for this step - just confirm and wait to see if anything changes after the cut (in case the manual has further steps, but this table only has one row per light, so single action should suffice).

```
wait()
```

|---|---|

| red | white |
| white | blue |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Turn 10, still no information received. Please respond with anything from the manual or from Deaf if you are receiving my messages.

Blind is not receiving instructions - this means Deaf may not have spoken to Blind yet, or Blind's messages to me aren't reaching the intended path properly. I cannot speak to Blind directly (I'm Mute), so I cannot answer Blind myself. Only Deaf can speak to Blind.

I need to push Deaf again to actually relay the instruction to Blind, since Deaf confirmed understanding but may not have realized they need to *speak* it to Blind (Deaf might be waiting for something else, like confirming with me first, which they did).

I'll gesture again to Deaf urging them to tell Blind now.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎","👍"])
```
